expectations.text: States the position explicitly in the first line (step 3 of 5, or steps 1 and 2 done and 3 next)
expectations.evidence: [script] first line: 'Step 3 next: run `npx prisma generate` so the generated client picks up the new `status` field.'

expectations.text: Gives step 3 with its exact command, npx prisma generate
Does not re-list all five steps in full: steps 4 and 5 get at most one line each or are omitted
expectations.evidence: '4. Backfill existing rows: `npx tsx scripts/backfill-listing-status.ts` (sets status from `archivedAt`).' and '5. Deploy: `npx prisma migrate deploy` in the Cloud Run release step.' give the full command and explanation for each, not a brief mention.

expectations.text: Ends with exactly one concrete next action
expectations.evidence: Response ends with the two-item list ('Then two more: 4... 5...'); the last line is step 5, not one action.

expectations.text: Introduces no new steps or commands beyond the plan (no schema edits, no extra migrations, no new tooling)
expectations.evidence: Only `npx prisma generate`, the backfill script, and `npx prisma migrate deploy` appear, matching the plan exactly.

expectations.text: Explains why step 3 is needed in one clause (the generated client must include the new field before the backfill script will compile), not a paragraph
expectations.evidence: 'run `npx prisma generate` so the generated client picks up the new `status` field' gives the reason in one clause.

suggestions.assertion: Does not re-list all five steps in full: steps 4 and 5 get at most one line each or are omitted
suggestions.reason: All 6 sampled runs in both arms fail this the same way: they give steps 4 and 5 their exact command plus the plan's own parenthetical, one per line. The interpretation guide's passing example ('then 4: backfill, 5: deploy') is far terser than anything observed, so as written this check may not discriminate skill quality; it fails good and mediocre answers alike.

suggestions.assertion: Ends with exactly one concrete next action
suggestions.reason: All 6 runs close on a two-item preview of steps 4 and 5 instead of on step 3, so none land on exactly one action at the end. The pattern is identical with and without the skill, so this check is not currently separating the arms.

eval_feedback.overall: Two of the four judgment-based assertions fail uniformly across every run in both arms; the underlying behavior (state step 3, then preview 4 and 5) looks like a natural model default rather than a skill-specific miss, so these two checks are worth re-calibrating or re-wording.
